section_summary: This section follows American President Lines’ efforts to remit yen revenues from Japan between July and December 1939. Correspondence records its objections to delayed permits and exchange losses, the State Department’s diplomatic response, and a later improvement in remittances. Weekly yen-position statements, two exchange-rate telegrams, and cross-reference notes document the wider currency controls.

people.name: Carl F. Farbach
people.role: State Department recipient of report copies

people.name: William G. McAdoo
people.role: Chairman of the Board, American President Lines

people.name: Joseph C. Grew
people.role: American Ambassador in Tokyo; telegram signatory

subfiles.title: Remittance permits
subfiles.from: E. L. Matteson, General Agent, Kobe
subfiles.to: Executive Department, Shanghai
subfiles.about: Matteson reports how exchange-permit delays affect foreign shipping lines and merchants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Most foreign shipping lines and several merchants face delayed remittance permits. Matteson attributes the delays to inadequate exchange coverage.

subfiles.title: Japanese gold and foreign exchange resources
subfiles.to: Internal file
subfiles.about: The note points to a memorandum on Japanese gold and foreign exchange resources.
subfiles.summary: References a May 15 memorandum by Luthringer.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at August 25, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists unremitted June through August yen receipts and exchange losses.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥403,294.07 held in Japan without permits.

subfiles.title: Appreciation for arrangements to transfer blocked revenues
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Land thanks the Department for arrangements to transfer American President Lines’ blocked revenues.
subfiles.summary: Land expresses appreciation for the Department’s efforts.

subfiles.title: Exchange loss on impounded yen receipts
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McAdoo requests restitution for exchange losses and raises possible reciprocal action against Japanese shipping revenues.
subfiles.summary: He reports a $9,000 loss after the yen’s decline and asks whether treaties permit the United States to impound Japanese vessels’ receipts.

subfiles.title: Objection to a two-month remittance delay
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McAdoo objects to Japan’s proposed two-month lag for shipping-revenue transfers.
subfiles.summary: June receipts have been paid, but McAdoo calls the proposed delay an interest-free forced loan that exposes the company to exchange losses. He again seeks treaty grounds for reciprocal impoundment.

subfiles.title: Treaty provisions and reciprocal treatment of vessels
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McAdoo seeks information on treaty rights and renews his proposal concerning Japanese shipping receipts.
subfiles.summary: Citing French shipping’s success after threatened retaliation, he urges consideration of impounding Japanese vessels’ revenues.

subfiles.title: Department reply on Japanese yen revenues
subfiles.to: William G. McAdoo
subfiles.about: The Department declines to seek stronger remittance terms or reciprocal impoundment at that time.
subfiles.summary: Hull says diplomatic representations have secured regular transfers on improved terms. The Department sees no treaty basis for a precise exemption from exchange-control delays and doubts that existing law supports the proposed impoundment.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at September 1, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports unpermitted yen receipts and realized exchange losses.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥220,339.59 held in Japan and $3,200 in realized exchange loss.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at September 8, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement records outstanding receipts and a report that July receipts are being remitted.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥152,000 outstanding; July’s ¥101,339.59 is reportedly being remitted.

subfiles.title: Japanese concern over the New York–London cross rate
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Embassy reports Japanese consideration of changing the yen’s currency link.
subfiles.summary: Japan is concerned by the falling sterling-dollar cross rate and may detach the yen from sterling and link it to the dollar. An announcement is expected, but the measures remain uncertain.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Tokyo telegram no. 477
subfiles.from: State Department, paraphrasing American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.to: Internal circulation
subfiles.about: This paraphrase restates the Embassy’s report on a possible shift from sterling to the dollar.
subfiles.summary: Paraphrases telegram no. 477 on Japan’s possible change of currency link.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at September 15, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports outstanding receipts and receipt of July’s remittance.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥204,000 awaiting permits; July collections were remitted on September 13.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at September 22, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports outstanding September receipts and receipt of August’s remittance.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥160,000 awaiting permits; August collections were remitted on September 25.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of improved yen remittances
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: McAdoo welcomes payment of August receipts and accepts the Department’s decision to defer further representations.
subfiles.summary: He says settlement in the month after accrual would satisfy the company and promises to report any deterioration.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at September 29, 1939
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists September yen receipts still lacking a remittance permit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥272,000 held in Japan.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at October 6, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists September and early October receipts without a permit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥309,000 awaiting remittance permits.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at October 13, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement distinguishes outstanding Kobe receipts from Yokohama receipts already remitted.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥271,000 outstanding; Yokohama’s September receipts were remitted on October 13.

subfiles.title: Yen pegged to the United States dollar
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Grew reports Japan’s decision to link the yen to the dollar effective October 25.
subfiles.summary: Japan sets the yen-dollar telegraphic transfer selling rate at 23-7/16 cents.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at October 20, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports a renewed delay in the promised Kobe remittance permit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥284,000 outstanding and a postponed permit for Kobe’s September receipts.

subfiles.title: Peiping exchange rates after the yen-dollar link
subfiles.to: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Lockhart reports North China’s currency announcement and local exchange rates.
subfiles.summary: North China authorities announce a dollar link consistent with parity between Federal Reserve Bank currency, the yen, and Manchukuo dollars. The telegram contrasts official and open-market rates.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at October 27, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement records October receipts for which no permit has been issued.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥101,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at November 3, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists unpermitted October and early November receipts.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥94,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at November 10, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement updates unpermitted yen receipts.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥106,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at November 17, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists November receipts awaiting a permit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥30,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: Japanese banks’ exchange transactions in the United States
subfiles.to: Internal file
subfiles.about: The note points to a Tokyo telegram about Japanese banks’ exchange rights after treaty lapse.
subfiles.summary: References Grew’s telegram citing a Tokyo Asahi article.

subfiles.title: Liquidation of commercial liabilities before a new treaty
subfiles.to: Internal file
subfiles.about: The note points to a company letter proposing a condition for a new commercial treaty.
subfiles.summary: References Electrical Research Products’ proposal to require liquidation of commercial liabilities.

subfiles.title: Difficulty obtaining exchange for coffee balances
subfiles.to: Internal file
subfiles.about: The note points to a Brazil despatch on Antonio Alvaro de Assumpcao’s Japanese balances.
subfiles.summary: References negotiations to obtain exchange for balances accumulated in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at November 24, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement lists November receipts without a remittance permit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥80,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at December 1, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports November receipts still awaiting permission to remit.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥60,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at December 8, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement adds early December receipts to November’s unpermitted balance.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥76,000 outstanding.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at December 15, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department; copy to Carl F. Farbach
subfiles.about: The statement reports December balances and a remittance received on December 18.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥71,000 in receipts and a ¥59,000 remittance.

subfiles.title: Discontinuation of weekly yen-position reports
subfiles.from: Arthur B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department
subfiles.about: Poole proposes ending weekly reports because yen conversion has become reasonably satisfactory.
subfiles.summary: Permits have arrived before the end of the month following each month’s receipts. Poole will report any renewed difficulty and thanks the Department for its assistance.

subfiles.title: American President Lines yen position at December 22, 1939
subfiles.from: A. B. Poole, American President Lines
subfiles.to: State Department
subfiles.about: The final statement records December receipts while noting that earlier collections have been remitted.
subfiles.summary: Reports ¥114,000 in December receipts; all earlier collections have been remitted.
